chunk_map.heading: The product box keeps the agents on course

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 line 8: "Point the agents at it." Closest to violating: "it" resolves to "the box" in the prior sentence (line 6) and the header; "the agents" is the header's own noun. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.

line 4-10: grep for positional callbacks (earlier/opening/last module/the X lecture) finds none; the slide points at no other file. Closest: line 6 "with your press release behind it" names an object, not a file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: line 8: "Before an overnight digest ranks what matters, or a new opportunity is written up" is a hypothetical, not "the X you did/saw"; no backward reference to a beat to verify.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess/predict beat and no live-demo scene

rules_evaluated.evidence: line 4-10: single chunk carries a self-contained claim (drift, the box as reference, point agents at it, keep it current). Closest: line 10 "Keep the box current." is a short paragraph but the slide is not orphaned.

line 1 header "The product box keeps the agents on course" vs body line 6-8: box as reference, agents compare work to it. Closest: header says the box keeps agents on course unconditionally while line 10 says a stale one steers wrongly; line 6 "can be that reference" conditions it, so the header is a true summary.

grep body for "Not X. Not Y." triples, anaphora, superlatives, number+retraction: none. Closest: lines 8-10 three short sentences ("Point the agents at it." / "Keep the box current." ) are different moves, not anaphora; line 8 "however well it reads" is concrete.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: body_view greps banned_words, ritual_ceremony, leverage_verb, session_biography CLEAN. Closest: line 6 "reference" and "press release" are ordinary engineering/product vocabulary, not repo dialect; line 4 "drifts" is plain.
